title: Enriched exponentials descend coherently to the nerve
statement:
Work in nested universes large enough for the following objects, and use locally Kan simplicial categories and the homotopy coherent nerve as in [def-coef-coherent-nerve-infrastructure], coherent mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and coherent adjunctions as in [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a simplicial category all of whose mapping simplicial sets $\mathcal A(U,V)$ are Kan complexes. Suppose its underlying ordinary category has chosen terminal object $1$, binary products with projections, and for every $X,Y$ a chosen object $E(X,Y)$ with evaluation $e_{X,Y}:E(X,Y)\times X\to Y$. Suppose the projection maps induce isomorphisms of simplicial sets
$$\mathcal A(T,1)\cong\Delta^0,\qquad\mathcal A(T,U\times V)\cong\mathcal A(T,U)\times\mathcal A(T,V),$$
and that product with $X$ followed by composition with this actual evaluation induces an isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\mathcal A(T,E(X,Y))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A(T\times X,Y)$$
for every $T,X,Y$. Then the chosen product and exponential assignments extend to simplicial enriched functors $\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and $E:\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ with enriched natural evaluation, and the displayed exponential isomorphisms are enriched natural in all three variables. For enriched morphisms $u:X'\to X$ and $v:Y\to Y'$, the action $E(u,v)$ is the transpose of $v\circ e_{X,Y}\circ(1\times u)$; in each simplicial degree the common parameter is shared by its diagonal. The coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal A$ has the indicated terminal object and products and, for every $X$, $N_{\mathrm{hc}}E(X,-)$ is a coherent right adjoint to product with $X$. Its counit is the image of $e_{X,Y}$ and its mapping-space adjunction is
$$\operatorname{Map}(T,E(X,Y))\simeq\operatorname{Map}(T\times X,Y),$$
induced by evaluation and composition, coherently natural in $T,X,Y$. In particular this asserts an adjunction of coherent functors, retaining higher homotopies, rather than only an adjunction of ordinary homotopy categories.

source.place: Kerodon Remark 7.7.3.9 (Tag 05UP), conditions (1)-(3) and conclusion; enriched action and its naturality make explicit the exponential universal property used there. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For enriched arrows $f:U\to U'$ and $g:V\to V'$ define $f\times g$ as the unique inverse image of $(f\pi_U,g\pi_V)$ under the assumed product isomorphism with source $U\times V$. More precisely this is a map $\mathcal A(U,U')\times\mathcal A(V,V')\to\mathcal A(U\times V,U'\times V')$ of simplicial sets, obtained using the two projections and composition. Composing with either target projection checks $(f'\times g')(f\times g)=(f'f)\times(g'g)$ and $1\times1=1$; injectivity of the product isomorphism proves these equalities on whole mapping simplicial sets. Thus these chosen products give an enriched bifunctor with enriched natural projections. In degree $n$ the pair $(f,g)$ has one common $\Delta^n$ parameter; every repeated occurrence is obtained by its diagonal. Faces and degeneracies commute with the construction because projection, composition and the inverse of a simplicial isomorphism do.

Write $\Theta_{T,X,Y}(a)=e_{X,Y}(a\times1_X)$ and $\lambda_{T,X,Y}=\Theta_{T,X,Y}^{-1}$. For a pair of enriched arrows $u:X'\to X$, $v:Y\to Y'$, put
$$E(u,v)=\lambda_{E(X,Y),X',Y'}\bigl(v e_{X,Y}(1_{E(X,Y)}\times u)\bigr).$$
This defines a simplicial map $\mathcal A(X',X)\times\mathcal A(Y,Y')\to\mathcal A(E(X,Y),E(X',Y'))$: first form the indicated composite using the product map of step 1, then apply the inverse simplicial isomorphism. Its defining equation is
$$e_{X',Y'}(E(u,v)\times1_{X'})=v e_{X,Y}(1\times u).$$
All these equations are equalities of simplicial maps; no choice of a transpose is made separately in individual degrees.

source.place: Condition (3); construction of the enriched exponential action.

proof.text:
If $u':X''\to X'$ and $v':Y'\to Y''$, the twofold application of the last equation, followed by the product composition identity, gives
$$e_{X'',Y''}((E(u',v')E(u,v))\times1_{X''})=v'v e_{X,Y}(1\times uu').$$
The right side also untransposes $E(uu',v'v)$. Injectivity of $\Theta_{E(X,Y),X'',Y''}$ gives $E(u',v')E(u,v)=E(uu',v'v)$. Untransposing $E(1,1)$ gives $e_{X,Y}$, which also untransposes $1_{E(X,Y)}$; hence $E(1,1)=1$. This proves the enriched functor axioms for $E:\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$. The defining equation in step 2 is the naturality equation in $Y$ and the dinaturality equation in the exponential variable $X$ for evaluation.

For arbitrary enriched arrows $t:T'\to T$, $u:X'\to X$, $v:Y\to Y'$ and $a:T\to E(X,Y)$, the equations already proved give
$$\Theta_{T',X',Y'}(E(u,v)a t)=v\,\Theta_{T,X,Y}(a)\,(t\times u).$$
Indeed substitute the defining equation of $E(u,v)$ into the left side and use $(1_{E(X,Y)}\times u)(a t\times1_{X'})=(a\times1_X)(t\times u)$ as maps $T'\times X'\to E(X,Y)\times X$. Equivalently both sides are $v e_{X,Y}(a t\times u)$. This equality is on the product of all four mapping simplicial sets, so it proves enriched naturality in all three variables, including simultaneous parameters. Inverting $\Theta$ gives the same naturality for $\lambda$.

source.place: Condition (3); naturality, including the shared simplicial parameter.

proof.text:
Fix $X$ and write $L(T)=T\times X$, $R(Y)=E(X,Y)$. Put $\eta_T=\lambda_{T,X,LT}(1_{LT})$ and $\epsilon_Y=e_{X,Y}$. Step 4 gives enriched naturality of $\eta$ and $\epsilon$. The equation $\epsilon_{LT}L(\eta_T)=1_{LT}$ is exactly the defining equation of $\eta_T$. To check the other triangle, apply the injective map $\Theta_{RY,X,Y}$. Naturality gives
$$\Theta_{RY,X,Y}(R(\epsilon_Y)\eta_{RY})=\epsilon_Y\Theta_{RY,X,LRY}(\eta_{RY})=\epsilon_Y=\Theta_{RY,X,Y}(1_{RY}).$$
Thus $R(\epsilon_Y)\eta_{RY}=1_{RY}$. These are strict enriched natural transformation identities, not identities only after taking components.

source.place: Condition (3); enriched unit, counit and both triangle identities.

proof.text: The definition of the nerve gives $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(B\times C)=N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\times N_{\mathrm{hc}}C$: a functor from each coherent simplex to the product is precisely a pair of functors. For the discrete enriched ordinal $[k]$, an enriched simplex into it is uniquely its nondecreasing sequence of object images, so $N_{\mathrm{hc}}[k]=\Delta^k$. Reversing vertex order and each mapping subset identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(B^{\mathrm{op}})$ with $(N_{\mathrm{hc}}B)^{\mathrm{op}}$. For an enriched natural transformation $\alpha:F\Rightarrow G:B\to C$, define $H:B\times[1]\to C$ using $F,G$ on the same-end mapping complexes and $H(b,0;b',1)(h)=\alpha_{b'}F(h)=G(h)\alpha_b$ on the cross complexes. The naturality equality checks mixed compositions; the other compositions are those of $F,G$. Thus $N_{\mathrm{hc}}H$ is an actual map $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\times\Delta^1\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}C$, with component $\alpha_b$. For composable $\alpha,\beta$, use $B\times[2]$ with cross maps $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\beta\alpha$; the same equality checks composition and gives a $2$-simplex in the internal functor simplicial set. This construction commutes with whiskering by its formula. Apply it to step 5: the two strict triangle identities give $2$-simplices with long edges the degenerate identities. These supply the required coherent unit, counit and triangle witnesses for $N_{\mathrm{hc}}L,N_{\mathrm{hc}}R$.

source.place: Explicit nerve and enriched-interval construction; coherence of the adjunction maps.

proof.text:
Set $D=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal A$. The locally Kan hypothesis and the coherent-nerve comparison give that $D$ is a quasicategory, together with the composition-compatible mapping-space comparisons. They identify $\operatorname{Map}_D(T,1)$ with the point and identify the map induced by the chosen projections
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(T,U\times V)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_D(T,U)\times\operatorname{Map}_D(T,V)$$
with the assumed enriched product isomorphism, up to the stated natural equivalences. Therefore $1$ is terminal by the definition of terminal object. For the discrete shape of two points, its internal functor simplicial set is $D\times D$, directly from its definition, and its mapping spaces are the twofold products. The mapping-space limit criterion of the cited cone-calculus node now makes the chosen projection cone a product cone. The coherent product functor is the nerve of the enriched product functor of step 1.

source.place: Conditions (1)-(2); mapping-space recognition of the terminal object and binary product.

proof.text:
Apply the adjunction-mapping-equivalence node to the two coherent functors and the actual triangle simplices of step 6 (their functor categories are quasicategories by the cone-calculus node). It supplies mutually inverse equivalences of the full mapping-space bifunctors in $T,Y$. In the orientation of the question the equivalence is
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(T,RY)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_D(LT,Y),\qquad a\longmapsto\epsilon_Y L(a).$$
Its inverse is $b\mapsto R(b)\eta_T$. The nerve comparison preserves actual edges and enriched composition with its coherent homotopies. Consequently the displayed forward map is the image of $a\mapsto e_{X,Y}(a\times1_X)$, and the inverse is its transpose. In particular its counit component is the specified evaluation edge, not an unspecified equivalent evaluation.

source.place: Condition (3); full coherent mapping-space adjunction and its prescribed formula.

proof.text: It remains to verify the universal-arrow clauses in the definition of coherent adjunction. The comma category $(L\downarrow Y)$ is the pullback along $L$ of source evaluation from arrows with fixed target $Y$. This source evaluation is a right fibration by the cited arrow-target node; its pullback is again one, by restricting the same horn lifts. Its fiber over $T$ is the arrow mapping space $U_D(LT,Y)$, identified with the specified mapping space by the pinch-comparison node. The right-fibration morphism-space formula identifies maps from $(T,b)$ to $(RY,\epsilon_Y)$ with the homotopy fiber at $b$ of $a\mapsto\epsilon_Y L(a)$. This map is the equivalence in step 8, so every such fiber is contractible by the homotopy-fiber criterion. Hence $(RY,\epsilon_Y)$ is terminal in $(L\downarrow Y)$. Apply the same argument in the opposite categories, with the roles of $L,R$ exchanged: the equivalence is then $b\mapsto R(b)\eta_T$, and it proves $(LT,\eta_T)$ initial in $(T\downarrow R)$. This proves precisely the two universal-arrow requirements, together with the coherent transformations and triangles already constructed.

source.place: Universal-arrow meaning of the coherent adjunction; explicit comma mapping spaces.

proof.text: The parameter $X$ also retains its higher naturality. The two assignments $P(T,X,Y)=\mathcal A(T,E(X,Y))$ and $Q(T,X,Y)=\mathcal A(T\times X,Y)$ are enriched functors $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A\to\mathbf{Kan}$: their actions are the pre/postcomposition maps constructed in steps 1-4. Their values are Kan by hypothesis. Step 4 says exactly that $\Theta:P\Rightarrow Q$ and $\lambda:Q\Rightarrow P$ are enriched natural transformations inverse on every mapping simplicial set. The enriched-nerve-transformation node, whose target is precisely $\mathbf{Kan}$, turns these into coherent inverse transformations of the corresponding space-valued diagrams, natural under products, opposites and restriction. Apply [lem-coef-enriched-hom-twisted-arrow-comparison] to $\mathcal A$. It identifies the nerve of its enriched Hom bifunctor with the intrinsic Hom diagram, including precomposition, postcomposition and all higher unit and composition homotopies. Restrict this identification along $(T,X,Y)\mapsto(T,E(X,Y))$ and $(T,X,Y)\mapsto(T\times X,Y)$. These restrictions identify the entire diagrams $N_{\mathrm{hc}}P,N_{\mathrm{hc}}Q$ with the two intrinsic mapping-space diagrams; the value comparison is the one in step 7. Thus this is the mapping-space equivalence of step 8 with coherent naturality in $T,X,Y$. Explicitly, its naturality equation for every simultaneous simplicial family is the equality of step 4; the interval and $[2]$ constructions in step 6 apply to these transformations and their inverse composites as well. Faces and degeneracies are restrictions of these actual simplicial maps. No passage to ordinary homotopy categories is used.

source.place: Construction 8.3.6.1 (03N6) and Proposition 8.3.6.2 (03N7): the nerve of enriched Hom is a Hom-functor. Restrict its coherent parameter diagram along the two enriched functors constructed in steps 1-4; combine with the enriched transposition identity of Kerodon 05UP condition (3).

proof_origin.place: Explicit proof of conditions (1)-(3), with enriched transpose and interval constructions; existing DAG mapping-space and comma recognition results supply the non-elementary inputs.
